title: RoomKit conformance scenario
description: One scenario of the shared conformance suite: a setup, the kit's calls, and what the RFC says they come to. Records (rooms, events, messages, contents, hook results) are written in the RFC's serialized form (§1.4). conformance/README.md defines how a runner reads each member.

id.description: The scenario's path under scenarios/, without .json.

rules.description: The RFC's rules the scenario checks, in the RFC's terms: "§10.1 step 9", "§7.5 rule 2", "§9.5.1 Reentrance", "Appendix B.2". The checker resolves each at the pinned RFC commit.

reentrancy.description: The cells of the reentrancy table (README, "Reentrancy cells") the scenario exercises.

record.description: A record in the RFC's serialized form; a reader takes an absent member as its default (§1.4).

router.description: A scripted router (§10.4), the kit's in place of the default: it answers every routed message with `room_id`, whoever sent it, an answer the kit holds to §10.1 step 2's rules; with a `gate`, it holds each routing there first.

identity_channel_types.description: The channel types identity resolution runs for (§11.4); absent, every type.

identity_timeout_ms.description: How long the resolver may take (§11.5); the implementation's default when absent.

delivery_backend.description: The kit's delivery backend (§22.2), the in-memory one, started with the kit: deliver() then queues its requests and the backend's worker executes them. Each member is a bound of its own; absent, the implementation's default.

verification_policy.description: The kit's identity verification policy (§11.7), the kit built with it: each member a bound or a switch of its own, the implementation's default when absent.

media_resolver.description: The kit's media resolver (§6.4), serving every AI channel registered on it: the bytes of each reference `media` names, in base64; none for another reference.

attached_media.description: The kit's attached-media reader (§6.4), serving every AI channel registered on it: the media an event carries outside its content are the media contents, in the serialized form, its metadata lists under `key`.

orchestration.description: The id of the scripted strategy the kit is built with as its default: every room it creates takes it unless the creation names another or none (§19.7).

delivery_gap_timeout_ms.description: How long a delivery lane waits on a cursor hole no lane runs, while no lane holds the room's delivery claim, before it forces the cursor past the hole and emits delivery_skipped (§13.5 Delivery lanes across processes); the implementation's default (30 s) when absent.

lock_manager.description: The kit's lock manager (§13.5): the in-memory one, whose release fails with `release_error` while a `lock_releases` step has set it failing, as a distributed lock that finds its lease expired.

release_error.description: What a failed release raises: its message.

inbound_rate_limit.description: The kit's inbound rate limit (§10.1): a token bucket per channel, full at first and holding at least one token, refilled at the most precise bound's rate; a message past it is refused, blocked with reason rate_limited, before anything is read or written. Absent, none.

persistence_policy.description: The kit's persistence policy (§14.3): the event types the kit's commits store. `persist_types`, when given, the only types stored; `exclude_types` never stored, whatever `persist_types` names. An event of a type it keeps out is delivered all the same, and consumes no index. Absent, every type is stored.

identities.description: Identities stored in the kit's store before the rooms are made (§5.6), each an Identity in the serialized form.

strategies.description: The scripted strategies the calls name (§19.7), none installed yet.

session_auditor.description: The run's session auditor (§15.8.2), the implementation's JSONL session auditor over a file of its own; with `attached`, attached to the kit before the steps, as the implementation's attach registers its hooks.

processes.description: Other processes serving the rooms (§19.7.5 rule 16): each a kit of its own over the run's store and lock manager, holding the setup's channels as objects of its own, a scripted agent answering from the one model of its channel id. A call's `kit` names the one it runs on.

channel.description: A scripted channel. Its parse is the default one (README, "Scripted channels"), its turn answers nothing and its delivery succeeds, unless a reaction says otherwise. An `ai` channel with a `model` is a scripted agent instead: the implementation's own AI channel over a scripted model (README, "Scripted agents").

type.description: A ChannelType, serialized (§6.2): sms, websocket, ai, host...

reads_usage.description: With `streams`: its `deliver_stream` also records what each generation tells of its usage (§6.1 deliver_stream, §6.4) as `{"usage": ..., "model": ..., "provider": ...}` under `streamed`. Without it, the channel skips it, as a reader that does not show usage does.

reads_loop_end.description: With `streams`: its `deliver_stream` also records the turn's end, the loop's `LoopEndMarker` the stream hands last (§6.1 deliver_stream, §6.4), as `{"loop_end": {"reason": ..., "rounds": ..., "usage": ...}}` under `streamed`. Without it, the channel skips it, as a reader that does not show how a turn ended does.

streams.description: Whether the channel takes a streamed response as it is written (§6.1 `supports_streaming_delivery`): its `deliver_stream` reads what it is handed, each item recorded under `streamed`, to the stream's end unless a reaction stops it.

deliver_stream.description: Reactions of a streaming channel's `deliver_stream` (§6.1), tried once per stream it is handed: `stop_after` stops its reading after that text delta or piece of reasoning, `fail` raises once it stopped.

on_room_attached.description: Reactions of the channel's `on_room_attached` (§6.1), tried once per call: `fail` raises, refusing the attach. Each call is recorded under `room_callbacks`.

on_room_detached.description: Reactions of the channel's `on_room_detached` (§6.1), tried once per call: `fail` raises. Each call is recorded under `room_callbacks`.

max_empty_retries.description: A scripted agent's max_empty_retries (Appendix A.9): how many times a round with no call to run is tried again, on a call its provider did not hand over or an empty answer after a round of calls; 1 when absent.

max_context_events.description: A scripted agent's max_context_events: the window of its default memory, a sliding window of the room's latest events (§20.3).

addresses.description: What the channel's own address methods answer (§5.7, §10.4), in place of the defaults, which write an address as given, name a message's conversation by its sender and record no recipient: `normalize_address` writes each address `normalizes` lists as its value, any other as given; `conversation_address` reads the message's metadata under `conversation_key`, a string not blank, else its sender; with a `recipient_key`, `reply_metadata` names the conversation under that key, `recipient_metadata` an address, and `recipient_address` reads a binding's value under it, or under `recipient_at`, written by `normalize_address`.

recipient_at.description: The binding metadata key `recipient_address` reads in place of `recipient_key`: a channel whose own method differs from what it declares. `recipient_metadata` and `reply_metadata` still write under `recipient_key`.

streams_in.description: The rooms the channel takes a streamed response in (§6.1 `supports_streaming_delivery_for`), asked whatever `streams` declares; in any other room it is delivered the answer whole. Absent, it streams wherever `streams` says.

recent_events_window.description: How many of the room's latest events the channel declares it reads (§6.1 `recent_events_window`), 0 by default.

sender_is_participant.description: Whether the channel names its own senders: its inbound `sender_id` is a room's `Participant.id`, not an address (§11.6), which no resolver is asked about.

serialize_room_turns.description: A scripted agent's serialize_room_turns: its turns in a room run one after the other, each reading the answers before it (§6.4, A room's turns one after the other).

steer_room_turns.description: A scripted agent's steer_room_turns: a message for a room where its turn runs is handed to that turn, read at its next stop, rather than a turn of its own (§6.4, A message for the running turn; §21.3). It implies serialize_room_turns.

human_input.description: A scripted agent's human_input_handler: the tools that ask a person (§9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED, where the other party is a human; §10.6.5 Human input). The agent declares `tools` and serves every name of `tool_names` itself, before its tools' handler, a name it does not define served when another of the agent's tools declares it; each call opens a request, which fires `on_user_input_required` and waits for its answer at most `timeout_ms` (300000 by default), bounded by that alone.

kit_tools.description: Tools the kit makes that a scripted agent is given as its own, among its tools (§23.4): `task_status`, the implementation's TaskStatusTool over the kit, and `cancel_task`, its CancelTaskTool, each reading the room and the channel of the call it serves, with their default windows.

tool_search.description: A scripted agent's tool_search (§6.4): true hides its catalogue behind find_tools and list_tools, false never does; null, the default, decides each turn from the catalogue's size.

tool_search_pinned.description: A scripted agent's tool_search_pinned: the names Tool Search never hides.

tool_search_threshold.description: A scripted agent's tool_search_threshold: the tool count past which Tool Search hides the catalogue when the model's window is unknown, and the most matches a search returns. 20 by default.

tool_search_threshold_pct.description: A scripted agent's tool_search_threshold_pct: the share of the model's window, in percent, past which the catalogue's schemas are hidden. 10.0 by default.

tool_search_miss_hint.description: A scripted agent's tool_search_miss_hint: what a search that finds nothing adds to its answer.

tool_search_threshold_tokens.description: A scripted agent's tool_search_threshold_tokens: the schema tokens past which the catalogue is hidden whatever the window; null sets no cap. 8000 by default.

tool_timeout_ms.description: A scripted agent's bound on each call of its tools (§21.6), in milliseconds; null bounds nothing. The implementation's default when absent.

tool_timeouts_ms.description: A scripted agent's bound per tool name (§21.6), in milliseconds, above its default and above a tool's own bound; null leaves that tool unbounded.

turn_budget_tokens.description: A scripted agent's budget of billed tokens per turn (§6.4): its input, output, cache read, cache creation and image tokens, counted as each generation reports them; past it the turn ends budget_exceeded at its next round boundary.

turn_budget_usd.description: A scripted agent's cost budget per turn (§6.4): each generation's usage priced at its model's catalogue price (`model.pricing`), added up; past it the turn ends budget_exceeded at its next round boundary. A model with no price refuses it.

system_prompt.description: A scripted agent's system_prompt (§6.4, Appendix A.9): what its turns' system prompt opens with, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets. None when absent.

temperature.description: A scripted agent's temperature (§6.4): how freely its model samples, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets; 0.7 when absent.

max_tokens.description: A scripted agent's max_tokens (§6.4): the most tokens a generation writes, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets. None when absent.

thinking_budget.description: A scripted agent's thinking_budget (§6.7, Appendix A.9): the tokens a turn may reason with, 0 stating off, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets. None when absent.

enable_thinking.description: A scripted agent's enable_thinking (§6.7, Appendix A.9): whether a turn reasons, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets, an off turning off a budget a less specific level set. None when absent.

thinking_coalesce_ms.description: A scripted agent's thinking_coalesce_ms (§6.7): how long its model's reasoning batches into one THINKING_DELTA, 0 publishing each piece; 80 when absent.

thinking_coalesce_chars.description: A scripted agent's thinking_coalesce_chars (§6.7): how many characters batch into one THINKING_DELTA; 256 when absent.

text_coalesce_ms.description: A scripted agent's text_coalesce_ms (§6.4): how long its answer's text batches into one TEXT_DELTA, 0 for none; 80 when absent

text_coalesce_chars.description: A scripted agent's text_coalesce_chars (§6.4): how many characters batch into one TEXT_DELTA; 256 when absent

publish_text_deltas.description: A scripted agent's publish_text_deltas (§6.4): whether a turn read as a delegated task's trace publishes its answer's text

publish_thinking_text.description: A scripted agent's publish_thinking_text (§6.7): whether its thinking events carry the reasoning's text to the room's subscribers; false when absent, which reads its length alone.

config_provider.description: A scripted agent's config_provider (Appendix A.9, per-turn settings): what it returns for each turn, as Python's AIChannelTurnConfig, by the room id of the binding it is called with, which the room of the context it is called with must carry; a room it does not name, or null, returns None (no per-turn configuration). A list gives that room's turns in order, one each, its last standing for the turns after.

skills.description: A scripted agent's skills (§24.3): its registry, each skill written to a directory of its own and discovered from there; an empty list is an empty registry, which is not none: a turn's registry is read only on an agent given one. None when absent.

skills_in_prompt.description: A scripted agent's skills_in_prompt (§24.3): whether its turns' system prompt lists the skills, whichever registry a turn reads; the instructions of the skills active are written either way. True when absent.

reasoning_effort.description: A scripted agent's reasoning_effort (§6.7): the effort its turns ask for, under the one its binding's metadata sets; null, as absent, sets none.

response_schema.description: A scripted agent's response_schema (§6.7, Appendix A.9): the JSON Schema each turn's answer must satisfy, under the one its binding's metadata or its config_provider sets; null, as absent, sets none.

retry_policy.description: A scripted agent's retry_policy (§6.4, a generation's retries): how many times a generation its provider refused as worth another try, before it handed anything, is tried again, each delay `base_delay_ms` times `exponential_base` to the attempt, at most `max_delay_ms`. No retry when absent.

fallback_model.description: A scripted agent's fallback_provider (§6.4): a second scripted model, asked once a generation's retries are spent on refusals worth another try, before anything was handed; its requests are under `<agent>/fallback` in `expect.models`.

max_author_images.description: A scripted agent's max_author_images: how many of the newest author images a turn sends as images, its history and its input counted together (§6.4), the rest read as a mention; null bounds nothing. 4 by default.

evict_threshold_tokens.description: A scripted agent's evict_threshold_tokens: the estimated tokens past which a tool's outcome reaches the model as a preview, its whole text stored for read_stored_result (§21.5). 5000 by default.

describe_empty_event.description: A scripted agent's describe_empty_event: the host's describer, asked of an event whose content reads as nothing in the turn's transcript (§6.4), which answers every event it is asked about with `says`; null keeps the event left out.

agent.description: A scripted agent built as an Agent (RFC §19.7) with this identity: its role, description and scope written at the end of its turns' system prompt as an identity block, in its language unless the room's conversation state sets one, unless identity_in_prompt is false. With a greeting and auto_greet (true unless set false), it greets each room a session starts in that binds it, once per room (§19.1).

audit.description: The auditor the agent's tool calls are recorded to (§15.8): its tool handler, serving every scripted tool, wrapped in the implementation's audit_tool_handler under the agent's id, recording to the run's tool auditor (`tool_auditor`) or to the run's session auditor through its tool_auditor bridge (`session_auditor`).

trigger.description: A HookTrigger, serialized: before_broadcast, after_broadcast, on_room_created...

reactions.description: Tried in order on each call: the first whose `when` matches is used, and used once unless it repeats. No reaction left: the default.

gate.description: Hold the call at this gate until a step opens it.

fail.description: Raise, with this message, once the actions ran.

response_metadata.description: In an `on_event` reaction: the record the channel's turn writes (§6.4, a ChannelOutput's response_metadata), which its caller's record reads.

error.description: In an `on_event` reaction: the error the channel met while producing its output, with this message (§6.1, a ChannelOutput's error): the output goes on, its response events kept, and the error surfaces as a raised one's (§9.3 ON_ERROR).

hold_after.description: In a `deliver_stream` reaction: the channel holds its read at `hold_gate` once it was handed the text delta this string equals, until a step opens the gate (§10.6.4).

hold_gate.description: The gate `hold_after` holds the read at.

stop_after.description: In a `deliver_stream` reaction: the channel stops reading the stream once it was handed the text delta or the piece of reasoning this string equals (§12.2 step 13s).

stop_after_rows.description: In a `deliver_stream` reaction: the channel stops reading the stream once it was handed this many of its rows, a call's start or end (§12.2 step 13s).

parsed.description: In a `parse` reaction: a patch on the event the channel builds (§10.1 step 4), what a channel reads off its own wire. Its members replace the built event's, those of its `source` the built source's; its strings name what the run made, as an action's arguments do.

refuse.description: In a `deliver` or `on_event` reaction: then the call fails with the provider's explicit refusal (§5.13): `error`, its words, `code` and `retryable`, what the refusal declares, and the `provider_message_id` it names.

after_turn.description: In an `on_event` reaction: actions the turn leaves to work it began, a task in the turn's execution context that makes them in order once the turn ended (§10.6.5): a verb of the turn's host then crosses as a `room_call`.

writes_record.description: In a hook's reaction: writes these keys on the turn's record, on `before_ai_generation` through its context's `response_metadata`, on another trigger through current_response_metadata(), when it answers one (§6.7).

hook_result.description: A HookResult (§9.4). A modify's `event` is a patch on the payload: its members replace the payload's.

action.description: A call a hook or a channel makes into the kit while it runs, in its execution context.

wait_for_lock.description: The room whose lock the calls wait for, or a reference to it ($r1).

waiters.description: How many calls wait for it; 1 by default.

lock_releases.description: Sets the releases of the kit's lock manager (setup.kit.lock_manager) failing or succeeding, from the next one on.

background.description: Start the call and go on; an `await` step reads its outcome.

kit.description: The process of `setup.processes` the call runs on; the run's own kit when absent. Taken by `process_inbound`, `install_strategy`, `uninstall_strategy`, `claim_room_strategy`, `room_strategy`, `room_strategy_is_current`, `speak_queue`, `listen_only`, `talk_again` and `close`.

defer_delivery.description: Returns at the commit, the call's completion handle (§10.1 step 18) named by the call's `as` label for `delivery.cancel` and `delivery.wait`.

meta.description: A WebhookMeta: provider, sender, recipient, body, external_id, timestamp, raw, media_urls, direction, event_type

require_structured_result.description: Inline runs only (§23.3): the agent hands its work back by calling the result tool, submit_result, served in the child room alone; a turn ending without the call is re-prompted with the tool's reminder, up to max_result_retries times, then the task's output is the tool's missing payload.

timeout_ms.description: The bound on the wait, the RFC's `timeout` in milliseconds (§10.6.5): null once it passes first. None by default.

handler.description: The name the later calls give the handler.

cache.description: The handler holds a CompletedTaskCache, of the implementation's default time to live.

targets.description: Each an id and its description or null: the tool build_delegate_tool builds. Absent: the generic one.

key.description: The delivery key the call cancels (§10.1 Explicit delivery cancellation).

reason.description: Why: the deliveries' cancellation reason; the implementation's default when absent.

channel_id.description: The intelligence channel whose running turns it steers.

room_id.description: The room whose turns it steers: every one for a Cancel, the most recent for any other directive; the channel's most recent turn when absent.

directive.description: A steering directive in the serialized form (§21.3): `{"type": "cancel", "reason": ...}`, `{"type": "inject_message", "content": ...}` or `{"type": "update_system_prompt", "append": ...}`.

of.description: The label of a deferred process_inbound whose handle it cancels.
The label of a deferred process_inbound whose handle it waits on.

orchestration.description: The id of the scripted strategy the room is created with, `null` for none; absent, the kit's default (§19.7).

handler.description: The name the later calls give the handler.

allowed_transitions.description: Each phase's phases a handoff may lead to, none constrained when absent.

known_agents.description: The targets taken though no binding of the room names them.

greeting_map.description: Each agent's greeting, none when absent: the handler's greeting_map, set once it is built.

event_channel_id.description: The channel a handoff's record is sent from, and what allows a greeting when the call names no channel.

targets.description: The custom tool's targets, each an id and its description or null; absent: the generic tool.

channel_id.description: What allows the greeting, the handler's event channel when absent, neither saying nothing. The channel itself is read only for a realtime session: the greeting reaches the whole room.

identity_id.description: The id of the identity the router is given, a known one.

trigger_id.description: The event the caller prepared for: a selection under the room lock that is another, or none, refuses the call trigger_moved.

kind.description: The kind of strategy asked about, the implementation's class of that name.

outcome.description: What a call comes to: its result, matched as an expectation, or its error. Neither given: the call must not fail.

error_name.description: What a call fails with, by its meaning in the RFC (README, "Errors").

contexts.description: Per room and scripted channel, the context each of its `deliver()` calls and, for an intelligence channel, each of its turns (`on_event()`) was handed, in order: `call` (`deliver` or `on_event`) and `recent_events`, the ids of its events, lifecycle records left out.

streamed.description: Per room and streaming channel, the items its `deliver_stream` read, in order: `{"text": ...}` for a text delta, `{"usage": ...}` for what a generation used when the channel `reads_usage`, `{"row": event}` for a stored row, `{"loop_end": ...}` for the turn's end when the channel `reads_loop_end`, `{"failed": true}` where the stream raised.

room_callbacks.description: Per room and scripted channel, the room callbacks the kit made (§6.1), in order: `{"call": "on_room_attached", "binding": ...}` with the binding it was handed, `{"call": "on_room_detached"}`.

ingested.description: Per room and scripted agent with a scripted memory, the events its memory was handed (§20 ingest), in order, matched as the timeline's events.

compacted.description: Per room and scripted agent with a scripted memory, the compactions between two tool rounds its memory was asked (§6.4, §20.1), in order: each `{history, usage}`, `history` the messages it was handed, each as `models` reads a request's, `usage` the round's token counters.

dispatch_turns.description: Per setup strategy with a scripted `dispatch`, the turns its policy was handed, in order: `room_id`, `event`, `recent` (each matched as the timeline's events), `speakers` (each [event id, label], in the order of `recent` then `event`), `candidates` (each `{channel_id, name, role, description, handle}`) and `asked`.

text_events.description: Per room, a minted one's as $r1, the TEXT_DELTA ephemeral events the room's realtime is handed, in order: each {text, round, channel_id}

thinking_events.description: Per room, the THINKING_START, THINKING_DELTA and THINKING_END ephemeral events its subscribers read (§6.7), in order: each `{type, thinking_length, round, channel_id}`, and `thinking` for an agent that publishes its text.

models.description: Per scripted agent, each generation's request as the model received it, in order: the `messages` it carries, each `{role, text, parts}` (`parts` its text and image parts in order, each `{text}` or `{image, mime_type}`, null for a text content), the `tool_results`, each `{tool_call_id, name, content, is_error}` (`name` the tool of its call, `content` a text, or a result's text and image parts in order, written as `parts`), its `system_prompt`, its `temperature` and `max_tokens` (§6.4), its `reasoning_effort`, `thinking_budget` and `enable_thinking` (§6.7), its `response_schema`, null for none (§6.7), and the names of the `tools` it declares, in order.

participants.description: Per room, the participants the store holds (§5.5), in the store's order.

resolver.description: The scripted resolver's calls, in order: the `room_id` of its context, the message's `channel_id` and `sender_id`.

media_resolver.description: The kit's media resolver's calls (§6.4), in order: the `url` of each media it is asked for and the `room_id` of the turn that asks.

ai_events.description: Per room, the framework events an AI channel's turn emits (§8.2, Level 1: `before_ai_generation`, `ai_response`), in emission order, matched as `framework_events`.

tool_audit.description: The run's tool auditor's entries in the order it recorded them, each with its entry's members (§15.8.3); its JSONL file holds one line per entry, those members.

session_audit.description: The run's session auditor's entries in the order it recorded them, each with its entry's members (§15.8.3); its JSONL file holds one line per entry, those members.

acp_wire.description: Per ACP channel, the requests and notifications its scripted agent received, in order: each `{method, params}`, `params` as the client wrote them (README, "Scripted ACP agents").

concurrent_call.description: A call of a concurrent step: started with the others, and waited for with them, so never in the background.

model.description: A scripted model: its answer to the agent's n-th generation of the run is its n-th round. A generation past the last round fails the turn.

chat_dialect.description: The implementation's Chat Completions rendering each of the model's requests is also written through, kept as `chat_messages` under `models` (§6.4, what a provider renders of a replayed round's reasoning): `openai`, a generic server's, or `deepseek`, `minimax` or `kimi`, that vendor's. Not rendered when absent. The model still answers from its rounds.

vision.description: Whether the model sees images (§6.4, a provider's supports_vision): false by default.

response_schema.description: Whether the model takes a response schema (§6.7, a provider's supports_response_schema): false by default. The model then keeps the provider's contract, as the implementation's mock provider does: a request under a schema it cannot take is refused before it is made, unsupported, and no request is kept; a round that calls no tool and does not end on a call its provider could not hand over is checked, a finish_reason of refusal refused, one that ran out of room truncated, any other text not the JSON document the schema asks for invalid_json; a streamed round's check comes before its done event, which the error replaces.

response_schema_with_tools.description: Whether the model takes a response schema beside tools (§6.7, a provider's supports_response_schema_with_tools): false by default.

pricing.description: The model's catalogue price (§6.7, a provider's catalog_entry().pricing): Python's ModelPricing, per million tokens, which a cost budget prices each generation at (§6.4). No price when absent.

verified.description: The day the price was read, YYYY-MM-DD.

context_window.description: The model's input context window in tokens (§6.7, a provider's catalog_entry().context_window), which Tool Search measures a catalogue against (§6.4). Unknown when absent.

name.description: The model's name (§6.7, a provider's model_name), which a turn's record names as ai_model (§6.4): scripted when absent.

provider.description: The provider's name (§6.7, a provider's name), which a turn's record names as ai_provider (§6.4): scripted when absent.

model_round.description: One generation's answer: its text, the calls it makes, why it stopped, and what it used; or its text, then a failure.

thinking.description: The round's reasoning, in the pieces the model streams it before its text (§6.1 deliver_stream, §6.7): a streaming channel reads each non-empty piece as `{"thinking": ...}`, in order, and no other channel reads it. The store holds none of it.

deltas.description: The round's text, in the pieces the model writes it, waiting between two, so a reader is handed each apart (§10.6.4): in place of `text`.

fails.description: The model fails with this message once it wrote its text, before its calls and its end: the response stream raises (§12.2 step 13s).

done.description: Whether the round's response stream ends with its done event (default true): false ends it after its text and its calls, without one.

gate.description: The model holds the round at this gate, before it writes anything, until a step opens it.

refuses.description: The provider refuses the request once the model wrote its text, before its calls and its end: an error it does not retry, with this HTTP status and message (§6.4).

context_overflow.description: Whether the provider classes the refusal as a context too long for the model (§6.4, a provider error's `context_overflow`); unclassed when absent.

provider.description: The provider that refuses, by its name (a provider error's `provider`); none when absent.

retryable.description: Whether the provider says the refusal is worth another try (a provider error's `retryable`, §6.4): false by default.

failure_after_calls.description: Whether the round's `fails` or `refuses` comes after its calls (default false): the model writes its text, then its calls, then fails, never reaching its end.

failure_after_done.description: Whether the round's `fails` or `refuses` comes after its done event (default false): the model writes its text, then its calls, then its end, then fails.

stream.description: The round's events in the order the model streams them, in place of `text`, `deltas`, `thinking` and `calls` (§6.4): a piece of reasoning, its `thinking` empty for a block's signature or redacted data alone, the `block` a vendor names it with; a piece of text; a call.

whole_response.description: The round is a whole response, as a provider that does not stream returns it (§6.4): its text and calls as the round gives them, its reasoning read from these members, handed to the loop first.

model_call.description: A call the round makes. `cut`: the response was cut short over its arguments, which never arrived whole (§6.4); only a round's last call, under a finish_reason that cuts calls.

metadata.description: Provider-owned data of the call (a thought signature), which goes back with it when the round is replayed (§6.4).

scripted_skill.description: A skill a scripted registry holds (§24.1): a directory named after it holding its SKILL.md, whose frontmatter gives `name` and `description` and whose body is `instructions`, and each of `references` under its references/ directory, by file name.

turn_config.description: One turn's configuration (Appendix A.9, per-turn settings), Python's AIChannelTurnConfig: each setting under the binding's metadata and over the agent's own, a null or absent one not set. `tools` replaces the toolset the binding's metadata declares, the agent's own tools still added after it; `tool_handler` serves the host's tools for this turn alone, in place of the agent's handler: each a scripted tool answering its calls, a name it does not hold unserved. `skills` gives the turn a skill registry of its own (§24.3), written as a scripted agent's, in place of the agent's for this turn alone, an empty list an empty registry.

scripted_tool.description: A tool the scripted agent serves, declared with its definition, answering every call one way: `returns` a text; `raises` an error of a kind (§9.3: the model reads the kind, the observers the message); `fails` or `refuses` with words the model reads (§9.3); `hangs`, never answering; `declines`, served by nothing.

tags.description: The tool's tags: English keywords find_tools searches beside its name and description (§6.4).

changes_state.description: Whether the tool's definition declares that a call it answers may change what later calls read (§6.4, the anti-loop guard): false by default.

declines.description: The tool's handler declines every call as not its own (§21.4): a call served by nothing, which an `on_tool_call` SYNC hook may serve (§9.3).

gate.description: Each call is held at this gate until a step opens it, then answered as the tool's other member says.

declared.description: Whether the agent declares the tool among its own (§21.1), true by default: an undeclared tool is served by the agent's tool handler all the same, for a hook that declares it (§6.4, What the generation hooks see).

returns_json.description: The tool answers this JSON value, not a text: the model reads it as JSON (§6.7), an object's members in the order written; a list whose every item is a mapping in a part's exact shape (`{"type": "text", "text"}`, `{"type": "image", "url", "mime_type"}`) as those parts (§21.4).

returns_parts.description: The tool answers these content parts in order, each `{text}` or `{image, mime_type}` (§21.4): a text and the images a model that sees reads in the round (§6.4).

writes_record.description: Before it answers, each call writes these keys on the turn's record through current_response_metadata(), when it answers one (§6.7).

room_hook.description: A hook registered for one room (§9.1): what a registration for a room declares, a hook's name, trigger, execution, priority, fail_closed and needs_lock, with no filter and the default timeout.

trigger.description: A HookTrigger, serialized: before_broadcast, after_broadcast, on_room_created...

store_call.description: A call of the store's own interface (RFC §14.1), `store.` and the operation's name, with the operation's arguments by name: what the store answers, whatever the kit does.

identity_resolver.description: A scripted identity resolver (§11.1), the kit's: it records each call (`expect.resolver`), then answers with the first of its `answers` whose `when` holds, `{"status": "unknown"}` when none does.

resolver_answer.description: One answer of a scripted resolver, used once unless it repeats: it holds at its `gate` first, then raises with `fail`, or answers `result`, an IdentityResult (§11.1).

identity_hook.description: An identity hook (§11.2), registered apart from the hooks of §9.1: it records each call, its payload the event and the IdentityResult it is handed, then answers with its reaction's `result`, an IdentityHookResult (§11.3), or null with none.

identity_hook_reaction.description: A reaction of an identity hook: `when` as a hook's, used once unless it repeats; it holds at its `gate`, then raises with `fail`, or answers `result`. An `inject`'s `event` is a template, completed as a hook's injected event.

scripted_memory.description: A scripted agent's memory (§20), in place of its default: the room's latest `max_events` events as a sliding window reads them (§20.3, the agent's max_context_events by default), with the `messages` it built, read before them, the `notes` it retrieved for the turn alone and the `speakers` its messages name (§20.2). `compacts` scripts what it answers each compaction between two tool rounds (§6.4, §20.1). `budget_aware` wraps it in the implementation's budget-aware memory (§20.3), which trims the oldest events to what the window leaves once the rest of the turn is paid for.

compacts.description: What the memory answers each compaction between two tool rounds (§6.4, §20.1), the n-th its n-th item, nothing past the last: `null` hands back nothing, the turn left as it is; an object hands back its `messages` (each `role` and `text`), then the last `keep` messages of the history it was handed (default 0), or `fails` with that message. Each compaction it is asked is kept, which `expect.compacted` reads.

compacting.description: The compacting memory's `max_context_tokens`, `summary_ratio` (default 0.10), `safety_margin_ratio` (default 0.15) and `min_events` (default 5), wrapping the memory and the budget-aware one when given; its summarizer is `summarizer`.

summarizing.description: The summarizing memory's `max_context_tokens`, `tier1_ratio` (default 0.50), `tier2_ratio` (default 0.85), `truncate_chars` (default 2000), `summary_max_tokens` (default 1000) and `min_events` (default 5), wrapping the memories above it when given; its summarizer is `summarizer`.

summarizer.description: The scripted model a compacting or summarizing memory summarizes with: its n-th summary is its n-th round's text; `expect.models` holds its requests under `<agent>/summarizer`.

retrieval.description: The retrieval memory's knowledge `sources`, `max_results` (default 5) and `min_query_length` (default 3), wrapping the memories above it (§20.2): each source answers every search with its `results` (each `content`, `score`, default 0, and `source`, default empty), at most the search's limit, or `fails` with that message.

writes_record.description: Each read writes these keys on the turn's record through current_response_metadata(), when it answers one (§6.7).

strategy_step.description: What a scripted strategy's install does (§19.7), as a reaction does: it holds at its `gate`, makes its actions in order (`$room` the room it is installed in), then refuses the room with `refuse`.

gate.description: Hold at this gate until a step opens it.

refuse.description: Then refuse the room with this message: the strategy's own refusal, an `invalid_argument`.

strategy.description: A scripted strategy (§19.7), a host's own: the agents it names by their channel ids, which the kit holds, and what its install and its own uninstall step do.

id.description: How the calls name it; one object whatever the room it is installed in.

agents.description: The channel ids of its agents, each a channel the kit holds: attached to the room as intelligence channels before its install runs.

loop.description: The implementation's Loop (§19.7.4) in place of a scripted strategy, its agents named by the channel ids of scripted agents with an `agent` identity: the producer answers the room, each message's text its task, and its reviewers review each output in child rooms (§23.3) until they approve or the iterations run out. A strategy with a `loop` has no `agents`, `install` or `uninstall`.

agent.description: The producer's channel id: the agent the room's messages ask, whose turns in the room the loop takes.

reviewer.description: The one reviewer's channel id, as `reviewers` naming it alone.

reviewers.description: The reviewers' channel ids, in the order they review.

max_iterations.description: How many times the producer produces at most (default 3).

strategy.description: How several reviewers review (a WorkerStrategy): `sequential`, each one handed the feedback before it, or `parallel`, all at once on the same output; sequential when absent.

supervisor.description: The implementation's Supervisor (§19.7.3) in place of a scripted strategy, its agents named by the channel ids of scripted agents with an `agent` identity: the supervisor answers the room, its workers registered on the kit and never attached. With no `strategy`, the supervisor is given one `delegate_to_<worker>` tool per worker; with one, a single `delegate_workers` tool that runs the whole team, supervised step by step when sequential. A strategy with a `supervisor` has no `agents`, `install`, `uninstall` or `loop`.
The supervisor's channel id: the agent the room's messages ask, given the delegation tools in the room it is installed in.

workers.description: The workers' channel ids, in the order a sequential team runs them.

strategy.description: How the team runs (a WorkerStrategy): `sequential` or `parallel`; per-worker tools when absent.

share_channels.description: The channel ids of the room attached to each child room a delegation opens.

task_timeout_ms.description: Each worker's delegation budget, in milliseconds: the implementation's task_timeout (default 120 seconds).

max_revisions.description: How many times a sequential team's step is reviewed at most before it stops the chain (default 3).

auto_delegate.description: Whether the framework delegates each message itself (default false), in place of the delegation tools: the supervisor's turns in the room run the team, then the supervisor answers from their results. It needs a `strategy`.

refine_task.description: With `auto_delegate`, whether the supervisor first turns the message into the team's task (default true), else the team is handed the message's text.

refine_instruction.description: With `auto_delegate` and `refine_task`, the instruction the supervisor turns the message into a task with, in place of the implementation's own.

delegation_message.description: The message the implementation keeps for a delegation in the background (default its own; null for none).

wait_for_result.description: With no `strategy`, whether a `delegate_to_<worker>` call waits for its worker (default true), else it starts the worker in the background and answers at once.

async_delivery.description: With a `strategy`, whether a `delegate_workers` call answers at once, dispatched, and runs the team in the background, its results handed back to the supervisor (default false).

strategy_uninstall_step.description: What a scripted strategy's own uninstall step does (§19.7): it holds at its `gate`, then makes its actions in order, `$room` the room it is installed in.

gate.description: Hold at this gate until a step opens it.

conversation_router.description: A conversation router (§19.4), the implementation's ConversationRouter: its hook is the hook's handler, which records no call.

routing_rule.description: A RoutingRule (§19.4): the agent its conditions select, tried in ascending priority.

conditions.description: RoutingConditions, each absent for no condition, all of them holding for the rule to match.

handoff_options.description: What a handoff handler (§19.6) is built with: the router it serves, the aliases of its targets and the phase each target leads to.

swarm.description: The implementation's Swarm (§19.7): its agents named by their channel ids, its entry the first when absent.

pipeline.description: The implementation's Pipeline (§19.7.1): its agents named by their channel ids, each handing off to the next, the first the entry point, and the supervisor every event also asks.

discussion_live_agent.description: An agent given live to a discussion, not registered on the kit: its channel id and its display name.

scripted_dispatch.description: A scripted dispatch policy (§19.7.5 rule 18), the implementation's MockDispatchPolicy: each decision asked takes the next of `decisions`, a list of channel ids (reason `scripted`) or a decision whole, the last one repeating, and with none it decides what the message asks with no policy; it holds at `gate` and waits `delay_ms` first, then raises `error` when given. It records each turn it is handed, which `expect.dispatch_turns` reads by the strategy's id.

pipeline_options.description: What a ConversationPipeline (§19.5) is built with: its stages, the phase naming its default agent (the first stage's when absent), and its supervisor.

discussion_strategy.description: The implementation's Discussion (§19.7.5), installed through the kit: its agents named by their channel ids, its keywords; with done, done(room_id) answers what the last discussion.done call named, false until one.

acp_channel.description: The channel is the implementation's ACP agent channel (§6.4), RoomKit the ACP client, over a scripted ACP agent the runner serves in its own process on a pipe, at the wire's level (README, "Scripted ACP agents"). The channel's `type` is `ai`.

cwd.description: The channel's `cwd`, an absolute path, declared in each `session/new`.

acp_agent.description: The scripted ACP agent: what it answers each request of the client, at the wire's level (README, "Scripted ACP agents").

initialize.description: Its `initialize` answer: `protocol_version` (default: the client's), `closes_sessions`, whether it announces `session/close` in `agentCapabilities.sessionCapabilities` (default true), and `agent_info`, the `agentInfo` it sends as written (default none).

prompts.description: Its answer to its n-th `session/prompt` of the run, in order; a prompt past the last is answered `end_turn` with no update.

acp_prompt.description: What the scripted agent does with one prompt: held at its `gate` first when it names one, then each of its `updates` sent as a `session/update` of the prompt's session, then its answer: `error`, a JSON-RPC error, or else `stop_reason` and `usage`.

updates.description: Each a SessionUpdate as ACP writes it (`{"sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk", "content": {"type": "text", "text": ...}}`), sent in order.

usage.description: The answer's `usage`, as ACP writes it (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`...), none when absent.

error.description: The prompt is answered with this JSON-RPC error in place of a result.
